name: calendar
description: Standalone month-grid calendar with roving-tabindex keyboard navigation, min/max/disabled dates, and single or range selection — range mode adds a hover/focus preview of the span, preset ranges, range length bounds and 1–3 months side by side; extracted from date-picker so availability grids and range pickers can use it directly

changes.note: Date ranges, grown up. (1) Preview: once a range has a start, hovering a day — or moving keyboard focus to it — marks the span start→day with data-state="preview" and the day itself "preview-end", drawn lighter than the committed band and with a dashed end ring; the pointer leaving the grids clears it. (2) data-months="2" or "3" shows consecutive months side by side with one prev/next pair: the controller wraps the grid in generated [data-part="months"] > [data-part="month"] panels, each a [data-part="month-title"] plus a copy of the grid named by it (aria-labelledby); the months wrap to a stack when the row is too narrow, arrow keys and PageUp/PageDown cross month boundaries without a jump, and a multi-month view leaves leading/trailing cells empty so each date appears once. setMonths(n) changes the count at run time. (3) Presets: an optional [data-part="presets"] group of [data-part="preset"] buttons — data-value today, yesterday, tomorrow, last-N-days, next-N-days, this|last|next-week|month|year, or explicit data-start/data-end — selects the range (clamped to min/max), moves the view to it, marks the matching preset aria-pressed="true", and emits faqir:calendar-change with a `preset` field; a preset that cannot fit is disabled. They sit above the grid, and as a side rail from the lg tier up. (4) data-min-range / data-max-range bound the range length in days, inclusive: while an end is chosen, days that would break them are aria-disabled and named "unavailable". (5) An optional [data-part="summary"] (aria-live) reads the selection back: "Oct 12 – 18, 2026 · 7 days". (6) Accessibility: a day button is now role="gridcell" in a presentational <td>, so its aria-selected is an allowed attribute (axe aria-allowed-attr); every day of a committed range is aria-selected. A day's name adds "today" (localized), "range start", "range end", "in range" and "unavailable" to the full date, and the month label is aria-live="polite" (set by the controller when the markup does not). Month labels, day names and the summary are formatted with Intl in the nearest lang (en-US output is unchanged). (7) The in-range days are drawn as one continuous band with capped ends behind the days (each cell's ::before) instead of separate rounded squares; restyle it through --calendar-range-bg / --calendar-preview-bg. Existing markup, values and events behave as before.

Nested components keep their own parts. The stylesheet reached the header, month navigation, grid and days with descendant selectors, so a component nested inside with parts of the same name took this one's styles. Parts are root > header > month-label, nav-prev and nav-next (the header is optional, so they may also be the root's children), root > grid, and root > grid > tbody > tr > td > day for the days the controller renders. Every part rule is now a child chain from the root, with the hops in :where(), so no rule changes specificity. No change for markup that follows the template.

data-today="true" and data-outside="true" are now declared. calendar.js has always written both onto the day buttons it renders and calendar.css has always styled them, but no manifest named them, so nothing generated from manifests knew a day cell carries them. 0.8-10's undeclared-attribute rule now makes this class of drift impossible: an attribute a component's CSS selects on that its manifest never declares fails the registry gate.

presets.description: Optional group (role="group" with an aria-label) of preset buttons, placed before the header. A row of chips above the months; a side rail from the lg tier (64rem) up

preset.description: One preset inside presets. data-value names a relative range — today, yesterday, tomorrow, last-N-days, next-N-days (any N), this-week, last-week, next-week, this-month, last-month, next-month, this-year, last-year, next-year (weeks start on Sunday, the first column) — or data-start / data-end (YYYY-MM-DD) give a fixed one. The controller clamps it to data-min/data-max, sets disabled when it cannot be picked (empty, outside data-min-range/data-max-range, or a span in single mode) and aria-pressed="true" on the one matching the selection; a click selects it, shows it and emits faqir:calendar-change

header.description: Row holding the month navigation buttons and the month label. Without it, the label and buttons are the root's own children

nav-prev.description: Navigate to previous month; auto-disabled when the whole previous month is before data-min

nav-next.description: Navigate to next month; auto-disabled when the whole next month is after data-max

month-label.description: Displays current month and year (for several months the span, "October – November 2026", visually hidden while the panels show their own titles). aria-live="polite": the controller adds it if the markup does not

grid.description: Calendar grid with role=grid and an aria-label

grid-body.description: Body the controller fills with week rows of day buttons

months.description: Generated by the controller for data-months > 1: the row of month panels, in the grid's place (the authored grid becomes the first panel's). Wraps to a stack when the row is too narrow; destroy() puts the grid back. Never authored by hand

month.description: Generated: one month panel inside months — a month-title and a copy of the grid

month-title.description: Generated: the panel's visible month and year, and the accessible name of its grid (aria-labelledby). The header's month-label is then visually hidden and announces the span

day.description: Individual day button — generated by the controller, never authored by hand. role="gridcell" (its <td> is presentational), data-date="YYYY-MM-DD", an aria-label with the full date plus today / range start / range end / in range / unavailable, aria-selected on the selection, aria-disabled on a day that cannot be picked

summary.description: Optional live text after the grid (give it aria-live="polite"). The controller writes the selection into it — the full date, "Oct 12, 2026 – select an end date", or "Oct 12 – 18, 2026 · 7 days" — and restores the authored text when nothing is selected

range-start.description: First endpoint of a range selection (data-mode="range")

in-range.description: Day strictly between the selected range endpoints — aria-selected too, drawn as a continuous band

range-end.description: Second endpoint of a range selection

today.description: Today's date, written by the controller on the matching day button — rendered with a ring so it reads as a landmark even when another day is selected

outside.description: A leading/trailing day belonging to the adjacent month, written by the controller — dimmed, still focusable, and still selectable

preview.description: While a range has a start and no end: a day inside the span the hovered (or focused) day would close. Drawn as a lighter band than the committed range

preview-end.description: The hovered (or focused) day a pending range would end on — a dashed ring at the end of the preview band

methods.name: setValue
methods.description: Silent set — updates selection and view without emitting a change event.

methods.name: setMonths
methods.description: Show 1–3 consecutive months side by side; they wrap to a stack when the row is too narrow.

methods.name: isDisabled
methods.description: Whether a date (Date or YYYY-MM-DD) is outside min/max or listed as disabled.

disabled-dates.description: data-disabled-dates: comma/space separated YYYY-MM-DD dates that cannot be selected; in range mode no range (or preset) may span one

months.description: data-months: how many consecutive months to show side by side, 1–3 (they wrap to a stack on a narrow row). One prev/next pair moves them all by a month

min-range.description: data-min-range: shortest range in days, inclusive (3 = start and end at least two days apart). While an end is chosen, closer days are unavailable; presets shorter than this are disabled

max-range.description: data-max-range: longest range in days, inclusive; 0 is unbounded

start.description: On a preset (not the root): the first day of a fixed range, YYYY-MM-DD — with data-end, in place of a relative data-value

end.description: On a preset (not the root): the last day of a fixed range, YYYY-MM-DD; omitted, the range is the data-start day alone

faqir:calendar-change.detail_range: { start, end: 'YYYY-MM-DD', startObj, endObj: Date, preset? } — emitted when the range completes; `preset` is the data-value of the preset that picked it (null for a data-start/data-end one)

required_attrs: Generated: role="gridcell" on each day button, its <td> role="presentation"
aria-label on day buttons with full date, plus today / range start / range end / in range / unavailable
Generated: aria-selected="true" on the selected day, or on every day of a committed range
aria-disabled="true" on out-of-range or disabled days, and in range mode on days that would break data-min-range/data-max-range (kept focusable for the roving tabindex)
Month changes: aria-live="polite" on month-label (added by the controller when missing)
Presets: role="group" and an aria-label on presets; aria-pressed on each preset (kept by the controller)
Several months: aria-labelledby on each grid, pointing at its month-title (generated)

keyboard.Home: focus first day of the week
keyboard.End: focus last day of the week
keyboard.Enter/Space: select focused day — in range mode the first press sets the start, the second the end
keyboard.Arrows/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown (range,: moving focus previews the span start→focused day
keyboard.Tab: presets, nav buttons and the one focusable day (roving tabindex)
keyboard.Pointer: click a day to select (range: start, then end; an earlier day restarts); with a start chosen, hovering previews the span and leaving the grids clears it; click a preset to select its range
